content: Shared sources and tooling generate client and server contracts for the direct Godot-client and Go-game-server loop. Godot and Go exchange WebSocket packets directly for live gameplay; Go owns authoritative simulation, while Godot owns presentation and input. Rails is a parallel backend for Godot, the website, and Bruno, backed by Postgres and outside the real-time gameplay path. Rails owns durable account and business state and its persistence; Go does not own API persistence, and future server-to-API communication must use explicit internal endpoints.
title: Space Rocks service boundaries and gameplay authority
